job_steps.name: Call
job_steps.headline: The homeowner calls at night.
job_steps.body: Water is coming through the kitchen ceiling. The call center rep takes the address, the damage type and the insurer.

renter_variant.headline: The tenant calls at night.
renter_variant.body: Water is coming through the kitchen ceiling. The call center rep takes the address, then reaches the landlord or property manager, who approves the work and holds the insurance on the building.

job_steps.name: Dispatch
job_steps.headline: A crew is on its way.
job_steps.body: The dispatcher picks the nearest free crew and sends the job notes. The scheduler books the estimator for the morning.

job_steps.name: Arrival
job_steps.headline: The crew shuts off the water.
job_steps.body: The crew lead finds the main valve and closes it. Power goes off in the wet rooms.

job_steps.name: Source repair
job_steps.headline: The plumber fixes the pipe.
job_steps.body: A copper line in the wall split. The plumber cuts it out and replaces it. Drying can start now.

job_steps.name: Inspection
job_steps.headline: The estimator maps the moisture.
job_steps.body: A moisture meter and a thermal camera show where the water went. Kitchen, hallway and part of the bathroom are wet.

job_steps.name: Testing
job_steps.headline: The walls get tested before anyone cuts.
job_steps.body: The house was built before 1978. A tester samples the drywall, texture and paint for asbestos and lead.

record_line.label: Testing
record_line.value: Samples sent to the lab, cleared

job_steps.name: Photos and scan
job_steps.headline: Every room is photographed and scanned.
job_steps.body: The estimator scans each wet room into a floor plan. Photos show the damage before any work.

job_steps.name: Extraction
job_steps.headline: The crew removes water and wet materials.
job_steps.body: Technicians extract standing water. They cut out wet drywall and baseboards, and the debris goes to a dumpster.

job_steps.name: Drying
job_steps.headline: Machines run and readings go in a log every day.
job_steps.body: Air movers and dehumidifiers dry the framing. A technician logs readings each day until the materials reach their dry goal.

job_steps.name: Pack-out
job_steps.headline: The family's things go into storage.
job_steps.body: The contents team photographs, boxes and lists every item in the kitchen and hallway. Boxes go to a storage vault.

job_steps.name: Estimate
job_steps.headline: The estimate goes to the insurer.
job_steps.body: The estimator prices every line in estimating software. Photos, the floor plan and drying logs go with it.

job_steps.name: Approval
job_steps.headline: The adjuster approves the claim.
job_steps.body: The adjuster questions part of the estimate. The supplement coordinator sends the drying logs as proof, and the adjuster approves it.

job_steps.name: Rebuild
job_steps.headline: The house gets put back together.
job_steps.body: The permit is filed. Drywall goes up, then paint, flooring and new lower cabinets.

job_steps.name: Walkthrough
job_steps.headline: The family walks the finished house.
job_steps.body: The project manager and the homeowner check every room. Contents come back from storage.

job_steps.name: Paid
job_steps.headline: The invoice is sent and paid.
job_steps.body: Accounts receivable bills the insurer and the deductible. Collections follows up until the job is paid in full.

glossary.plain: The emergency work that stops damage from growing: removing water, soot or mold and drying the building.
Rebuilding what mitigation tore out: drywall, floors, cabinets, paint.
The person who decides what the insurance pays. A public adjuster works for the homeowner instead of the insurer.
Third-party administrator. A company that manages claims and contractor programs for insurers.
The estimating software many insurers and contractors use to price repairs line by line.
Extra charges sent to the insurer after the first estimate, with proof such as photos and drying logs.
Boxing up a family's belongings, listing them and moving them to storage during the work.
